_comment: Only static site content may be tracked in this public repo (ADO #1980, #1981). Everything tracked here is served from clearthemud.org. Deny wins over allow. Site generation code moved to the build repo on 2026-08-01 (ADO #1975); the deny entries under tools/ keep it from coming back. This list is checked at commit time by .githooks/pre-commit, which is only active in a clone where someone has run 'git config core.hooksPath .githooks', and which 'git commit --no-verify' bypasses. tools/tests/test_publish_allowlist.py re-checks this list against the tracked tree, and .github/workflows/tests.yml runs that check on every pull request and on every push to main. GitHub Pages publishes main, and as of 2026-08-01 main carries no branch protection and no required status check, so the workflow reports on a push rather than gating it.

allow.reason: Published candidate and race pages. This is the site's primary content, gated further by tools/data/do-not-publish.json.
Published per-state hub pages linking to the race directories below them.
GeoJSON district and county boundaries used by the map views. Public reference data from official sources.
Stylesheets served to the browser, including the dossier.css that all published pages link.
Client-side scripts served to the browser for map rendering and race table filtering.
Published methodology page explaining the source-tier model to readers of the site.

The site registry (races.json) and the two publication gate lists. Data, not code. The gate lists must stay because this repo's own pre-commit hook reads them from here and cannot reach across the repo boundary. races.json and the reference files stay pending an owner decision on inverting registry ownership; the build repo's converter reads races.json as ballot-status truth and its generators write it, all through site_data_dir().

Guards on published site content and on the two publication gate lists. These read the tracked tree through git, so they belong beside the repo they inspect. Tests for generation code went to the build repo with the code they cover.
The pre-commit promotion gate itself. Must be tracked so a fresh clone can install it.

The GitHub Actions workflow that runs tools/tests on pull requests and on pushes to main. Not served to readers, but it must be tracked here because GitHub only runs workflows that live in the repository they check.
Search engine sitemap for the published pages.
GitHub Pages custom domain binding for clearthemud.org. Removing it takes the site down.
Build and contribution instructions for this repo. Contains no internal research or findings.
Blocks private artifacts from being staged. Must be tracked for the protection to reach every clone.

deny.reason: Session status files and working docs are internal process records, not site content. Canonical copies live in the private clearthemud ADO repo under docs/status/.

Generates the state hub pages and sitemap.xml. Site generation code lives in the build repo's site_tools/ (ADO #1975); this entry stops a copy reappearing here, where the build repo's tests cannot see it and the two would drift.

Generates race and candidate HTML from build-repo dossier JSON. Site generation code lives in the build repo's site_tools/ (ADO #1975); this entry stops a copy reappearing here, where the build repo's tests cannot see it and the two would drift.

Builds the county and place SVG maps from Census shapefiles. Site generation code lives in the build repo's site_tools/ (ADO #1975); this entry stops a copy reappearing here, where the build repo's tests cannot see it and the two would drift.

End-to-end county buildout pipeline. Site generation code lives in the build repo's site_tools/ (ADO #1975); this entry stops a copy reappearing here, where the build repo's tests cannot see it and the two would drift.

Maps the WA SOS roster onto counties to produce county_races.json. Site generation code lives in the build repo's site_tools/ (ADO #1975); this entry stops a copy reappearing here, where the build repo's tests cannot see it and the two would drift.
Same migration (ADO #1975). The candidate validator ran against the roster registry and wrote an internal QA report, neither of which is site content.
Same migration (ADO #1975). Assigns incumbent and challenger roles in the registry; it is build-time logic, not a served file.
Same migration (ADO #1975). Turns the WA SOS filing roster into registry entries, reading a CSV that only exists in the build repo.
Same migration (ADO #1975). CLI for adding races and candidates to the registry and regenerating pages from it.
Internal QA output. The candidate-validation report enumerates matching defects and unresolved records, which is internal research rather than anything a site reader consumes.
Private collection artifacts. Note tools/data/ is a different path and stays allowed; this entry is the repo-root data directory that .gitignore also anchors against.
Internal agent operating instructions. Describes collection workflow and is not site content.
Local agent configuration, which can carry internal paths and prompts. Never site content.
